title: Integral dg ABC data and normalized triangulated H0 realizations
statement:
Let $\mathcal A$ be a small cochain dg category over $\mathbf Z$, using the object set, Hom complexes of abelian groups, closed units and right-to-left bilinear composition of [def-coef-small-dg-category]. The Hom differential satisfies $d(ba)=d(b)a+(-1)^{|b|}b\,d(a)$. Write $Z(x,y)=\ker(d:\mathcal A(x,y)^0\to\mathcal A(x,y)^1)$.

Shift data (B) consist of dg functors $[n]$ for all $n\in\mathbf Z$, strictly satisfying $[0]=1$ and $[n+m]=[n][m]$ on objects and homogeneous arrows, and cochain isomorphisms $\phi_{n,x,y}:\mathcal A(x,y[n])\cong\mathcal A(x,y)[n]$. Here $V[n]^j=V^{j+n}$ and $d_{V[n]}=(-1)^n d_V$. Compatibility with composition means $\phi_n(ba)=\phi_n(b)a$ for $b:y\to z[n]$, and $\phi_n(g[n]a)=(-1)^{n|g|}g\phi_n(a)$ for homogeneous $g:y\to z$, $a:x\to y[n]$, with canonical degree identifications.

An admissible sequence consists of objects $x,y,z$, closed degree-zero arrows $a:x\to y$, $b:y\to z$, and graded degree-zero arrows $\pi:y\to x$, $s:z\to y$, satisfying $\pi a=1_x$, $bs=1_z$, $a\pi+sb=1_y$, $ba=0$, and $\pi s=0$. Its degree-one boundary is the actual element $\pi d(s)$. A dg biproduct of $x,z$ consists of an object and closed inclusions and projections with the two identity composites, two zero cross composites and sum-of-projectors identity. Axiom (A) means that a dg zero object exists (all Hom groups to and from it vanish in every integer degree), and every pair has a dg biproduct. For shift data as above and $f\in Z(x,y)$, a cone datum consists of an object $c$, an admissible sequence $y\xrightarrow{i}c\xrightarrow{p}x[1]$, and the exact equality $\phi_{1,x[1],y}(f[1])=\pi d(s)$.

A triangulated $H^0$ realization consists of a category on the literal object set of $\mathcal A$, with the additive, zero-object, shift, pre-triangulated and triangulated structures of [def-weil-triangulated-category], and surjective additive maps $q_{x,y}:Z(x,y)\to\operatorname{Hom}(x,y)$. They obey $q(f)=q(g)$ if and only if $f-g=d(h)$ for some $h\in\mathcal A(x,y)^{-1}$, carry units and composites to identities and composites, and induce the given shifts on objects and closed representatives. A triangle is distinguished if and only if it is isomorphic to $(x,y,z,q(a),q(b),q(\delta))$ for an admissible sequence and a closed $\delta:z\to x[1]$ with $\phi_1(\delta)=\pi d(s)$. Equivalently, it is distinguished if and only if it is isomorphic to $(x,y,c,q(f),q(i),-q(p))$ for a closed degree-zero $f$ and a cone datum as above. The realization is specified as data; its existence is not asserted in this definition.
